Verb of breaking-relationship / rebelling (1Ki 8:50; 12:19; 2Ki 1:1; 3:5,7; 8:20,22; 2Chr 10:19; 21:8,10; Job 8:4; 13:23; 33:9 (variant); 34:6,37 (variant); Pss 25:3; 37:38; 51:13 [11] (variant); 55:23 [22] (variant); 73:21 (variant); 89:33 [32]; 107:11 (variant); Pro 28:21; Isa 1:2,28; 24:20; 43:27; 46:8; 48:8; 53:12; 59:13; 66:24; Jer 2:8,29; 3:13; 33:8; Lam 3:42; Eze 2:3; 18:31; 20:38; Da 8:23; Hos 7:13; 8:1; 14:10 [9]; Am 4:4; Zep 3:11). 41 occurrences. Hyphenated. Within the OT moral-failure triad H2398 chata ('miss-mark sin'), H6586 pasha ('transgress-rebel'), H5771 avah ('iniquity-bend'). The kernel is the breaking-of-relationship (political 1Ki 12:19 'Israel rebelled against the house of David'; covenant Isa 1:2 'children I have raised, and they have rebelled against me'). Hyphenated to bridge the political-rebellion and covenant-rebellion.
